correctness.rationale: The all-zero preimage is the independent-set hard-core gas with activity \(\lambda=p/(1-p)\). The regular-tree cavity recursion \(r\mapsto\lambda/(1+r)^d\) has critical fixed point \(r=1/(d-1)\) and exact uniqueness activity \(d^d/(d-1)^{d+1}\). Above it, successive ball parities converge to two distinct cavity messages. The source cylinder has strictly increasing probability \(P_q(r)=r^q/((1+r)^q+\lambda)\), so Lemma 1 and Remark 2 of arXiv:2304.03102v2 transfer the parity gap to a second-layer quasilocality contradiction.

value.rationale: The source itself identifies the hidden hard-core phase transition as the mechanism behind loss of quasilocality and leaves its non-Gibbs threshold unspecified even though regular trees are included. On the regular tree, the exact hard-core threshold therefore gives a natural, structurally motivated sharp onset for the source witness. The result supplies an explicit all-order non-Gibbs region and a concrete binary-tree value \(4/5\) without overclaiming the unknown behavior below it.
